name: Bata Villa (Thomas Bata Foundation)
funding: Donations were CZK 4.48M in 2025: CZK 4.40M from founder Bata Schuh Stiftung, CZK 30k from Continental Barum. Subsidies: City of Zlín CZK 195k, Zlín Region CZK 35k.

name: Zikmund Villa
funding: Foundation set up by owner Čestmír Vančura. 2025 income CZK 4.2M: gifts 2.1M (including his foundation, NAVI CZ, ZULIP, MEJTA, Edhouse, PSG Construction), grants 1.0M, mainly EEA and Norway Grants.

name: 6th of October War Panorama
funding: Egypt's state commissioned it under President Mubarak and the National Military Museums Department runs it. North Korean architects helped build it; tickets cost 3 to 30 Egyptian pounds in 2010.

name: Villa Skeppet
funding: The Christine and Göran Schildt Foundation owns and runs it, and Christine Schildt sits on its board. Tickets cost EUR 22. No accounts or donor list is published.

name: Gallen-Kallela Museum
funding: The Akseli Gallen-Kallela Museum Foundation runs it. 2024 income EUR 0.80M: state subsidy 39%, municipal grants 26% (Espoo is a named supporter), tickets 21%, services and sales 14%.

name: Didrichsen Art Museum
funding: The Didrichsen Art Foundation, set up by the founders in 1963, runs it. 2024 income EUR 1.30M: tickets 50%, state subsidy 17%, other grants 16% (grantors not named), services 15%.

name: Muuratsalo Experimental House
funding: The Alvar Aalto Foundation runs it. The foundation's Alvar Aalto Museum reported 2024 income of EUR 2.73M: state subsidies 38%, tickets 19%, services and sales 19%, municipal grants 14%.

name: Villa Kokkonen
funding: The City of Järvenpää, owner since 1998, runs it. The first restoration phase, budgeted at EUR 425,000, drew on city investments and a EUR 105,000 culture ministry grant.

name: Hvitträsk
funding: State money. A site of the National Museum of Finland, a department of the Finnish Heritage Agency under the Ministry of Education and Culture. Adult ticket EUR 15.

name: Villa Mairea
funding: The Villa Mairea Foundation runs it. A. Ahlström Kiinteistöt Oy owns and maintains the building. No income, grant or donor list is published on the foundation's site.

name: Fondation Hartung-Bergman
funding: A public-utility foundation created by decree in 1994 runs it. No funder is named on its site. Its subsidiary HB Projet hires the site out for events and filming.

name: Maison Louis Carré
funding: The Association Alvar Aalto en France, founded in 2006 to buy and manage the house, runs it. The Finnish and French culture ministries and the Île-de-France Region are named supporters.
